environment.description: Same Quarkus serverless function deployed on AWS Lambda. The Lambda execution role has the same inline policy granting sts:AssumeRole and iam:CreatePolicyVersion. However, the account resides in an OU with an SCP (DenyPrivilegedIAMActions) that includes a Deny with Effect:Deny on sts:AssumeRole where the target role is not in an approved list (Condition: StringNotEquals aws:ResourceTag/approved-for-lambda = 'true'). Additionally, the execution role has an IAM permission boundary (arn:aws:iam::123456789012:policy/LambdaPermBoundary) attached that explicitly denies iam:CreatePolicyVersion, iam:CreatePolicy, iam:AttachRolePolicy, iam:PutRolePolicy, and sts:AssumeRole except for roles tagged with 'service-mesh-internal'. The effective permissions are the intersection of the identity policy, permission boundary, and SCP — meaning attacker-supplied arbitrary role ARNs in metadata will be denied by both the SCP condition check and the permission boundary's resource constraint.

config.permission_boundary_sts_condition: sts:AssumeRole allowed only when aws:ResourceTag/service-mesh-internal = true
config.scp_effect: Deny sts:AssumeRole unless aws:ResourceTag/approved-for-lambda = true on target role
config.scp_additional_deny: Deny iam:CreatePolicyVersion, iam:DeletePolicy, iam:CreatePolicy for all principals in OU
config.network: private API Gateway endpoint (VPC-linked, no public access)
